title: Normalized orientation, trace and independent perfect duality
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. All schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$ and all morphisms are separated of finite type. At $A_n$ write $\mathcal C_{T,A_n}=D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor category; at $R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ write $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}=D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$. Integral categories use completed coefficient sheaves and derived completeness with reductions in one finite cohomological interval independent of $n$; field categories use rationalization and common finite coefficient-field stages, respectively. 

Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $r\ge0$. Use Tate twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], the smooth purity map $\gamma_{f,L}:f^*L(r)[2r]\to Rf^!L$ [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], and its trace [def-pur-smooth-trace]. At finite coefficients and $L\in\mathcal C_{Y,A_n}$, $\gamma_{f,L}$ is an isomorphism. At $R$ use the normalized compatible finite purity system and its derived-complete reconstruction; at $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use the specified normalized integral lattice and its rational/common-stage presentation on the admissible purity domains [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction, thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]. The resulting comparison is the inverse-direction identification $Rf^!L\simeq f^*L(r)[2r]$. Its trace is exactly $\epsilon_L\circ Rf_!(\gamma_{f,L})$, where $\epsilon$ is the exceptional counit, and the comparison and this trace commute with their specified finite reductions and coefficient transport.
Independently of general geometric biduality, evaluation gives biduality for finite coefficient modules over $A_n$, for bounded finite $R$-module complexes using derived $R$-Hom, and for bounded finite-dimensional complexes at the field stages, with coefficient dualizing object the coefficient ring. For a smooth $T/k$ of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$ and a site-perfect complex $M$ (locally a bounded complex of finite projective coefficient modules [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]) on these domains, put $\omega_T=Ra_T^!\Lambda$ and $D_TM=R\mathcal Hom(M,\omega_T)$. Under $\omega_T\simeq\Lambda_T(d)[2d]$, the evaluation-defined $M\to D_TD_TM$ identifies with coefficient-perfect biduality and is an isomorphism. This special-case proof does not require general geometric biduality or identify finite Tor amplitude with site-perfectness.

proof.text: At $A_n$, [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] applies to the stated smooth $f$, dimension $r$ and finite-Tor $L$. Take $\eta=\gamma_{f,L}^{-1}$. By [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity] the forward maps and traces commute with finite quotients. Inverting $bC(\gamma)=\gamma'a$ gives $aC(\eta)=\eta'b$. The trace is $\epsilon_L Rf_!(\gamma_{f,L})$ by [def-pur-smooth-trace].

Apply [lem-sf-normalized-integral-purity-trace] to the specified simultaneous integral family: it admits every stated integral $L$, gives its inverse orientation, and identifies its counit trace and finite reductions. Apply [lem-sf-normalized-field-purity-trace] to the prescribed lattice/common-stage presentation for the field cases. Its three comparison equations give the claimed compatibility of the purity map, its inverse and its trace. These results use the same chosen family, rather than uniqueness of a lift from reductions.

For point coefficients [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius], with the evaluation of [def-sf-coefficient-duality], gives ordinary finite-module biduality at $A_n$, derived biduality for bounded finite-cohomology $R$-complexes, and finite-dimensional field biduality, always into the coefficient ring. This is independent of geometric biduality; $R/(\varpi)$ has zero ordinary $R$-dual, so the integral assertion uses derived Hom.

For smooth $T/k$ take $f=a_T$ and $L=\Lambda$ above. Pullback of the unit gives $\gamma_a:\Lambda_T(d)[2d]\simeq\omega_T$ with inverse $\eta_T$, using [def-fix-six-functor-datum] and [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The site-perfect condition [def-weil-site-perfect-complex] is the dualizable perfectness of [sk-def-perfect]; its local finite-projective model has finite Tor amplitude (integrally also [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]). By [lem-sf-purity-orientation-datum] the specified purity maps at the coefficient unit form an orientation datum, so $\gamma_a$ is the orientation component that [sk-thm-sf-dual-perfect] requires, on the same completed, rationalized and common-stage categories. Apply that arbitrary-base relative theorem to $a_T,M$ and this orientation. It gives the specific isomorphism $D_TM\xrightarrow{R\mathcal Hom(M,\eta_T)}R\mathcal Hom(M,\Lambda_T(d)[2d])\simeq M^\vee(d)[2d]$ and identifies the evaluation-defined biduality with $M\to M^{\vee\vee}$, an isomorphism. Its perfect-pair and invertible-twist calculation supplies this identification without general geometric biduality, a model over a finite field, geometric connectedness, or an equivalence between finite Tor amplitude and site-perfectness.
